recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Divide by cos²θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. The sinθcosθ term blocks any single-ratio substitution, but dividing the whole equation by cos²θ turns every term into a tangent or a secant.

recall.must_convey: That the equation is divided by cos²θ, giving sec²θ + tan²θ = 3 tanθ.

steps.why: A term in sinθcosθ cannot be written in one ratio directly, but divided by cos²θ it becomes a plain tanθ. That is why this family goes to tangent.
common_mistakes: Dividing by cosθ only and leaving a mixed term.
Trying to substitute sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ, which does not remove the product term.

steps.label: Convert sec² and factorise
steps.margin_note: Second mark. sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ turns it into a quadratic in tanθ, which then factorises.

recall.must_convey: That sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ gives the quadratic 2tan²θ − 3tanθ + 1 = 0, which factorises.
accept: sec squared is one plus tan squared so it becomes two tan squared minus three tan plus one equals zero and factorises

steps.why: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 is the identity that pairs with the Pythagorean one. It is what lets a secant be removed without introducing a cosine.
common_mistakes: Failing to collect the two tan² terms.

steps.label: Solve the first root
steps.margin_note: Third mark. tanθ = 1 is tan(π/4). For a TANGENT equation the general solution is nπ + α — no ± and no (−1)ⁿ.
lines: Now tanθ = 1 = tan(π/4), so α = π/4
For tanθ = tanα, θ = nπ + α

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = 1 gives α = π/4 and the TANGENT general solution θ = nπ + α.
accept: tan theta equals one is tan pi by four so theta is n pi plus pi by four
for tangent the general solution is n pi plus alpha
the first family is n pi plus pi by four

steps.why: Tangent repeats every π rather than every 2π, which is why its general solution is the simplest of the three — just nπ + α.
common_mistakes: Using 2nπ ± α for a tangent equation.
Adding a (−1)ⁿ that does not belong.

steps.label: Solve the second root
steps.margin_note: Last mark. tanθ = 1/2 is not a standard angle, so the principal value stays as an inverse tangent — that is the exact answer and is expected.
lines: Here the principal value is α = Tan⁻¹(1/2)

lines.text: ∴ θ = nπ + π/4  or  θ = nπ + Tan⁻¹(1/2),  n ∈ Z

recall.must_convey: That tanθ = 1/2 gives α = Tan⁻¹(1/2), and that BOTH families are reported.

steps.why: Both roots of the quadratic are valid tangents — a tangent can take any real value, unlike a sine — so unlike the twin question nothing is rejected here.
common_mistakes: Trying to force 1/2 into a standard angle.
